# Deprecated!

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/adapters/convex.mdx

title: Convex Adapter
description: Convex Adapter for Better Auth.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/convex" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/adapters/convex" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/convex" />

# Deprecated!

Please do not use this in any new projects. We recommend checking out https://github.com/get-convex/better-auth

## Why?

This adapter uses hacks and work-arounds in order for everything to work, which is not sustainable.
A more official implementation around Better-Auth and Convex made by those who are more familiar with the Convex ecosystem
is now available, so I recommend using that instead.

A Convex adapter for Better Auth which allows your Better Auth instance to communicate with your Convex DB.

**Note:** This isn't full Convex integration, meaning hosting your Better Auth endpoints on Convex is not possible with this library.

<Callout type="warn">
#### Limitations
If you encounter any issues, please report them in the [Issues](https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/issues) section.

Please note that Convex DB is not inherently designed for this purpose. I have implemented workarounds to facilitate dynamic queries and mutations within Convex, which is typically not supported. Additionally, there are several limitations that may affect the functionality of BetterAuth in certain scenarios. Some plugins may not operate as expected.

Here are the key limitations to consider:
- **Performance Issues**: Due to the inability to perform dynamic queries/mutations, we send a request to Convex Actions, which then calls the mutate/query function. This results in at least two calls, not including subsequent database queries or mutation calls.
- **Lack of `sortBy` Support**: BetterAuth requires sorting at the individual field level, while Convex only supports sorting at the table level.
- **Degraded Performance for Pagination Queries**: Convex's support for pagination is limited, which may lead to performance issues when working outside its intended scope.
- **No Support for Certain Operators**: Operators such as `starts_with`, `ends_with`, or `contains` are not supported. This limitation primarily affects the admin plugin. (As far as I'm aware.)

<Callout>
#### Benefits

* If you don't mind the extra requests to make a DB query/mutation and the other limitations, then this adapter is for you!
* Convex doesn't support dynamic queries/mutations, however we've built a workaround to allow Better Auth to use dynamic queries/mutations on Convex DB. 
This also means that you can leverage the power of our dynamic queries/mutations in your codebase if you wanted to as well! Read more [here](#utilizing-the-better-auth-adapter).
* And lastly, if you love Convex, and you really want to use Better Auth, then this adapter is currently the best bet.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @better-auth-kit/convex
```

## Usage

<Steps>

<Step>

### Initiate the Convex Database Adapter

Head over to your Better Auth server instance, and under `database`, add the `convexAdapter` function.

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { convexAdapter } from "@better-auth-kit/convex";
import { ConvexHttpClient } from "convex/browser";

const convexClient = new ConvexHttpClient(process.env.CONVEX_URL);

export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: convexAdapter(convexClient),
  plugins: [],
  //... other options
});
```
</Step>

<Step>

### Create the Convex Handler

This allows our adapter to communicate with your Convex DB.

Create a new file in `convex/betterAuth.ts` and add the following code:

**NOTE:** It's important that the file name is exactly `betterAuth.ts` and that it is in the `convex` directory.

```ts
import { action, internalQuery, internalMutation } from "./_generated/server";
import { internal } from "./_generated/api";
import { ConvexHandler, type ConvexReturnType } from "@better-auth-kit/convex/handler";

const { betterAuth, query, insert, update, delete_, count, getSession } = ConvexHandler({
  action,
  internalQuery,
  internalMutation,
  internal,
}) as ConvexReturnType;

export { betterAuth, query, insert, update, delete_, count, getSession };
```

<Callout type="info">
  If you're receiving type errors, make sure that you're running `convex dev` for Convex to generate the types.

</Step>

</Steps>

That's it! You're all set up! 🔥

## Important Notes

1. When using Better Auth with Convex, we recommend not using your `auth` instance in any Convex files.
Unexpected errors may occur, as Better Auth isn't designed to be used in Convex enviroments.

2. If you have mutations or queries which require session verification, check out the [Verifying a user's session in a Convex function](#verifying-a-users-session-in-a-convex-function) section.

3. Better Auth doesn't have Convex integration, meaning you can't host your Better Auth endpoints on Convex.
You'll have to use a supported integration from Better Auth to host your endpoints. To Better Auth, Convex would just be your database.

## Verifying a user's session in a Convex function

You can verify a user's session in a Convex function by using the `getSession` query.

It requires that you pass the `sessionToken` to the query, which you can get from the user's session data.

```ts
const session = await ctx.runQuery(internal.betterAuth.getSession, {
    sessionToken: "the user's session token",
});
```

```ts title="Example"
export const deleteMessage = mutation({
	args: { messageId: v.id("chat"), sessionToken: v.string() },
	handler: async (ctx, args) => {
		const session = await ctx.runQuery(internal.betterAuth.getSession, { // [!code highlight]
			sessionToken: args.sessionToken, // [!code highlight]
		}); // [!code highlight]

		if (!session) {
			throw new Error("Unauthorized");
		}

		const message = await ctx.db.get(args.messageId);
		if (!message) {
			throw new Error("Message not found");
		}

		await ctx.db.delete(args.messageId);
	},
});
```

## Utilizing the Better Auth adapter

Because of the way this adapter works, you actually get a really cool benefit of being able to use Convex DB dynamically.
Unlike traditionally, where you must predefine Convex functions to either do queries or mutations, you can now do so dynamically at runtime.

```ts title="Example"
import { auth } from "./auth.ts";

const adapter = (await auth.$context).adapter;

// Create a row
await adapter.create({
	model: "user",
	data: {
		name: "some-user",
		email: "some-user@example.com",
		password: "password",
	},
});

// Update a row
await adapter.update({
	model: "user",
	where: [{
		field: "name",
		value: "some-user"	
	}],
	update: {
		name: "some-other-name",
	}
})

// Update multiple rows
await adapter.updateMany({
	model: "user",
	where: [{
		field: "name",
		value: "some-user"
	}],
	update: {
		name: "some-other-name",
	}
})

// Delete a row
await adapter.delete({
	model: "user",
	where: [{
		field: "name",
		value: "some-user"
	}]
})

// Delete multiple rows
await adapter.deleteMany({
	model: "user",
	where: [{
		field: "name",
		value: "some-user"
	}]
})

// Count number of rows
await adapter.count({
	model: "user",
	where: [{
		field: "name",
		value: "some-user"
	}]
})

// Get a row
await adapter.findOne({
	model: "user",
	where: [{
		field: "name",
		value: "some-user"
	}]
})

// Get multiple rows
await adapter.findMany({
	model: "user",
	where: [{
		field: "name",
		value: "some-user"
	}]
})
```

## Schema generation

Traditionally, you'd use the `@better-auth/cli` to generate the schema for your database.
However, in some cases, you may import your `auth` instance into your Convex files, which includes this Convex adapter.
And for us to allow schema generation from the Better Auth CLI, we'd need to use our schema generation code apart of our adpater,
which includes the utilization of the node `fs` module. 

Convex doesn't support the usage of the `fs` module in it's native enviroment, so this will cause build errors.

To get around this, we intend to build a custom CLI specifically for schema generation, which will be available in the `@better-auth-kit/cli` package.

Keep an eye out for this in our [roadmap](/roadmap).

## Using JWT plugin in Convex

The JWT plugin in Better Auth doesn't work off the bat in Convex, this is due to certain algorithms not being supported in Convex's Enviroment.

We recommend using the `RS256` algorithm, which is supported in Convex.

```ts
export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: convexAdapter(convexClient),
  plugins: [
    jwt({
      algorithm: "RS256",
    }),
  ],
});
```

For a minimal repo implementing this, check out [this repo](https://github.com/juliusmarminge/convex-betterauth/tree/main) by <GithubUser>juliusmarminge</GithubUser>.

# database-explorer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/cli/database-explorer.mdx

title: Database Explorer
description: A Better-Auth powered database explorer and schema visualizer.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/cli" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/cli" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/cli" />

The database explorer is a powerful tool that provides visibility into your Better-Auth connected database.
It features an intuitive schema visualizer that helps you understand table relationships and
track which fields originate from specific plugins, making database management and troubleshooting more efficient.

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ## Run the CLI
    Make sure you're in your project directory and run the following command:

    ```package-install
    npx @better-auth-kit/cli db
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step>
    ## That's it!
    You can now view your database and schema visualizer by running the above command.
    
    <Callout>
    If you're running into any issues with the database explorer not being able to get your schema, make sure that you have any extensions such 
    as ad-blockers or others that could be blocking any requests disabled.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Database Explorer
<img src="/docs/db-explorer-database.png" alt="Database Explorer" className='dark:block hidden border border-border' />
<img src="/docs/db-explorer-database-light.png" alt="Database Explorer" className='dark:hidden drop-shadow-lg' />

## Schema Visualizer
<img src="/docs/db-explorer-schema.png" alt="Database Explorer Schema" className='dark:block hidden border border-border' />
<img src="/docs/db-explorer-schema-light.png" alt="Database Explorer Schema" className='dark:hidden drop-shadow-lg' />

## FAQ

### Does it work for all databases?

The database explorer works for any database that is supported by Better-Auth. If your DB adapter works for Better-Auth, the database explorer will work.

### How does it work?

The database explorer works by reading your better-auth configurations, and appends a custom plugin, as well as special configurations
to your auth instance. It then uses an express server hosting that auth instance with CORS rules specific to authorizing `https://better-auth-kit.com` to 
fetch the data.

### Why doesn't it have every table or field in my database?

We only know what tables and fields are available in your database by utilizing Better-Auth's schema system based on your auth instance.
This means that if you have any custom tables or fields, the database explorer will not be able to show them, unless specified in the auth config.

### Why does it say that my table row count is only 100?

It's possible that it's a limitation of your database adapter. Some databases may not have support for counting rows, which can be the cause of this.
If you believe that this is not the case, please open an issue where the database adapter comes from.

# seed.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/cli/seed.mdx

title: Seed
description: Seed your Better-Auth database with deterministic, yet realistic, fake data to populate your database.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/cli" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/cli" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/cli" />

<Callout type="warn">
    There is an existing bug, we're investigating it.

Our seeding tool allows you to generate realistic sample data, such as users, for your Better Auth database. Inspired by [Drizzle Seed](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/seed-overview).

<Steps>

<Step>
## Install

```package-install
npm install @better-auth-kit/seed
```

</Step>

<Step>
##  Create

Create a `seed.ts` file next to your `auth.ts` file

<Tabs items={[ "Adding users", "Custom Table" ]}>
<Tab value="Adding users">
Learn more about adding users [here](#adding-users).

```ts title="seed.ts"
import { Seed, users } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    // Adds 100 users (including sessions and accounts)
    ...users(),
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Custom Table">

You can add any number of tables to your seed.

```ts title="seed.ts"
import { Seed, table, $ } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    // Adds 100 rows to the `myTable` table
    myTable: table({
        id: $.uuid(),
        user: $.foreignKey({ model: "user", field: "id" }),
        name: $.firstname(),
    }),
    myOtherTable: table({
        id: $.uuid(),
        user: $.foreignKey({ model: "myTable", field: "name" }),
        state: $.states(),
        country: $.countries(),
    }),
});
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
<Step>
## Run 

```package-install
npx @better-auth-kit/cli@latest seed
```

And that's it! 🔥
</Step>
</Steps>

## Adding Users

Handles the creation of `user`, `session`, and `account` tables.

```ts
import { users, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...users() // [!code highlight]
});
```

You can modify or append new fields to the `user`, `session`, or `account` tables, as well as add custom types.

```ts
import { users, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    // Optional: pass in custom types for the tables
    ...users<{
        user: MyCustomUser,
        session: MyCustomSession,
        account: MyCustomAccount
    }>({
        user: { // [!code highlight]
            role: $.randomChoice( // [!code highlight]
                $.custom(() => "admin"), // [!code highlight]
                $.custom(() => "user"), // [!code highlight]
                $.custom(() => "super-admin"), // [!code highlight]
            ), // [!code highlight]
            banned: $.boolean({ probability: 0.5 }), // [!code highlight]
            banReason: $.custom(() => "Some hard-coded ban reason"), // [!code highlight]
            banExpires: $.randomDate(), // [!code highlight]
        }, // [!code highlight]
        session: { // [!code highlight]
            ipAddress: $.ip(), // [!code highlight]
            userAgent: $.userAgent(), // [!code highlight]
        }, // [!code highlight]
        account: { // [!code highlight]
            password: $.password(), // [!code highlight]
        } // [!code highlight]
    })
});
```

### Additional Options

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="User Count">

By default, we will generate 100 users. You can change this by passing the `count` option.

```ts
import { users, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...users({}, { count: 500 }) // [!code highlight]
});
```
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Custom Model Names">
You can change the model names directly in your auth config, and we will automatically pick up on that.
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Disable Sessions">

You can disable the creation of sessions by passing the `createSessions` option.

```ts
import { users, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...users({}, { createSessions: false }) // [!code highlight]
});
``` 

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Disable Accounts">

You can disable the creation of accounts by passing the `createAccounts` option.

```ts
import { users, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...users({}, { createAccounts: false }) // [!code highlight]
});
```
</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Adding Organizations

Handles the creation of the `organization`, `member`, `invitation` (if enabled), and `team` (if enabled) tables.

```ts
import { users, organizations, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...users(), // Require at least 100 users in your DB to create 100 organizations.  // [!code highlight]
    ...organizations() // [!code highlight]
});
```

You can modify or append new fields to the `organizations`, `members`, `invitations`, and `teams` tables, as well as add custom types.

```ts
import { organizations, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
     // Optional: pass in custom types for the tables
    ...organizations<{
        organization: MyCustomOrganization,
        member: MyCustomMember,
        invitation: MyCustomInvitation,
        team: MyCustomTeam
    }>({
        organization: { // [!code highlight]
            name: $.firstname(), // [!code highlight]
        }, // [!code highlight]
        member: { // [!code highlight]
            role: $.randomChoice($.custom(() => "admin"), $.custom(() => "member")), // [!code highlight]
        } // [!code highlight]
        //... // [!code highlight]
    })
});
```

### Additional Options

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Count">

By default, we will generate 100 orgs, members, invitations (if enabled), and teams (if enabled). You can change this by passing the `count` option.

```ts
import { organizations, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...organizations({}, { count: 500 }) // [!code highlight]
});
```
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Custom Model Names">

You can change the model names by passing the `modelName` option.

```ts
import { organizations, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...organizations({}, { 
        modelName: { // [!code highlight]
           organization: "organizations", // [!code highlight]
           member: "members", // [!code highlight]
           invitation: "invitations", // [!code highlight]
           team: "teams", // [!code highlight]
        } // [!code highlight]
    }),
});
```
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Enable Invitations">

You can enable the creation of invitations by passing the `createInvitations` option.

```ts
import { organizations, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...organizations({}, { createInvitations: true }) // [!code highlight]
});
``` 

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Enable Teams">

You can enable the creation of teams by passing the `createTeams` option.

```ts
import { organizations, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...organizations({}, { createTeams: true }) // [!code highlight]
});
```
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Disable Members">

You can disable the creation of members by passing the `createMembers` option.

```ts
import { organizations, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...organizations({}, { createMembers: false }) // [!code highlight]
});
```
</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Adding API keys

Handles the creation of API keys on the `apikey` table.

```ts
import { users, apiKeys, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...users(), // Require at least 100 users in your DB to create 100 api keys. // [!code highlight]
    ...apiKeys() // [!code highlight]
});
```

You can modify or append new fields to the `apikey` table, as well as add custom types.

```ts
import { apiKeys, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...apiKeys<MyCustomApiKey>({
        name: $.custom(() => "My API Key"), // [!code highlight]
    })
});
```

### Additional Options

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Count">

By default, we will generate 100 api keys. You can change this by passing the `count` option.

```ts
import { apiKeys, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...apiKeys({}, { count: 500 }) // [!code highlight]
});
```
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Custom Model Names">

You can change the model names by passing the `modelName` option.

The default model name is `apikey`

```ts
import { apiKeys, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    ...apiKeys({}, { modelName: { apiKey: "apikeys" } }) // [!code highlight]
});
```

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Multiple Seed Files

You can execute multiple seed files by creating a `seed` folder next to your `auth.ts` file.

<Files>
  <File name="auth.ts" />
  <Folder name="seed" defaultOpen>
    <File name="1-users.ts" />
    <File name="2-organizations.ts" />
    <File name="3-api-keys.ts" />
  </Folder>
</Files>
Within the `seed` folder, you can create any number of files, with any name you want, and they will be executed in alphabetical order.

```bash title="Terminal"
npx @better-auth-kit/cli@latest seed
```

By default, the CLI will prompt you to select which seed files to execute. However, you can pass the `--run-all` flag to execute all seed files.

```bash title="Terminal"
npx @better-auth-kit/cli@latest seed --run-all
```

## $ Functions

We have a number of functions that you can use to generate random data.

### Custom

This is a special function that allows you to hard code a value, and isn't used to generate random data.

```ts
import { table, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    myTable: table({
        greeting: $.custom(() => "Hello, world! This can be any value!"), // [!code highlight]
    }),
});
```

### Foreign Key

Generates a foreign key.
```ts
import { table, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    myTable: table({
        foreignKey: $.foreignKey({ model: "myOtherTable", field: "id" }), // [!code highlight]
    }),
});
```

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Unique">

You can pass a unique option to the `unique` option.

```ts
$.foreignKey({ model: "myOtherTable", field: "id", unique: true })
```

By default, the foreign key will not be unique.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

### Emails

Generates a random email address.
```ts
import { table, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    myTable: table({
        email: $.email(), // [!code highlight]
    }),
});
```

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Unique">

By default, we will generate a unique email address. You can change this by passing the `unique` option.

```ts
$.email({ unique: false })
```

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Domain">

By default, we will generate an email address with a random domain. You can change this by passing the `domain` option.

```ts
$.email({ domain: "example.com" })
```

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Fullname">

You can pass a fullname function to the `fullname` option to customize the email address. 

```ts
$.email({ fullname: () => $.first_and_lastname() })
```

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

### First Names

Generates a random first name.
```ts
import { table, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    myTable: table({
        firstName: $.firstname(), // [!code highlight]
    }),
});
```

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Modifier">

You can pass a modifier function to the `modifier` option.

```ts
$.firstname({ modifier: (name) => `${name} 🔥` })
```

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

### Last Names

Generates a random last name.
```ts
import { table, $, Seed } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

    myTable: table({
        lastName: $.lastname(), // [!code highlight]
    }),
```

- `past`
- `future`

By default, the date will be `any`.

## Configuration

You can export a `config` object to configure the seeding process.

```ts title="seed.ts"
import { Seed, type SeedConfig } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const seed = Seed({
    // Your seeding tables...
});

export const config: SeedConfig = {
    deleteRowsBeforeSeeding: false,
    rows: 100,
};
```

### `deleteRowsBeforeSeeding`

Delete all rows in the tables before seeding.

Default is `false`.

<Callout type="warn">
The table rows will be deleted in the order of the `models` array.

```ts
import { type SeedConfig } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const config: SeedConfig = {
    deleteRowsBeforeSeeding: {
        enabled: true,
        // Make sure to delete the tables in order of foreign key dependencies
        models: ["user", "session", "account"],
    },
};
```

### `rows`

The default number of rows to seed.

Default is `100`.

<Callout>
If a given table has a `count` option, that will take precedence over this.

```ts
import { Seed, type SeedConfig } from "@better-auth-kit/seed";

export const config: SeedConfig = {
    rows: 1000,
};
```

## Credit

This project was heavily inspired by [Drizzle Seed](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/seed-overview), and the datasets used in this project are from Drizzle Seed as well. Big thanks to the Drizzle team for the awesome work! 💖

# ui-components.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/cli/ui-components.mdx

title: UI Components
description: Generate UI components using the ShadCN registry for your project.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/cli" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/cli" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/cli" />

<Callout type="warn">
#### This feature is not yet available.
View our [roadmap](/roadmap) to see what is coming soon.

## Lore

Given that Better-Auth works around a plugin eco-system, it's important to have a way to extend UI and extend the components that build them.

We intend to provide a large set of UI components that builds off [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) components, and allow you to generate your auth components using the Better-Auth-Kit CLI. 
For each major component (such as a sign-in, or sign-up component), we will provide a base component that you can extend.
Using the example of sign-up, we will provide smaller components which you can then add to your sign-up component, such as our `<OAuth />` component.

This opens the door of opportunity for you to extend the components to your liking, and also develop smaller components for any plugin that may require UI to go along with it.
For example, with our [legal-consent](/plugins/legal-consent) plugin, we can then provide a component that allows you to collect the user consent.

## Usage

You can add any of our provided components to your project by using the following command:

```package-install
npx @better-auth-kit/cli@latest ui add <component-name>
```

## Components

We currently have the following components:

- `SignIn`
- `SignUp`
- `OAuth`

## Component Builder

We provide a [Components builder](https://better-auth-kit.com/components) page which allows you to easily view and customize the components,
allowing you to see what is possible, then run 1 command to add the component and your customizations to your project.

---

# introduction.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/introduction.mdx

title: Introduction
description: Information about Better-Auth-Kit

<img src="/banner/1600x600.png" alt="Better Auth Kit Banner" width="100%" />

Welcome to the documentation for Better Auth Kit! 👀

## What is Better-Auth-Kit?

Better-Auth-Kit is a collection of useful plugins, adapters, tools and examples all open source for the community to freely use on top of [Better Auth](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth).
The project is maintained by <GithubUser>ping-maxwell</GithubUser>, a core contributor to Better Auth, however it is not officially affiliated with Better Auth.

## What is Better Auth?

Better Auth is the most comprehensive authentication library for TypeScript. You can learn more about it [here](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth).

## Why make Better Auth Kit?

As a core contributor to Better Auth, I have been working on improving the library and adding new features.
However there are some plugins, packages or other things that are not suitable for the main Better Auth library.

I decided to create a separate library to house these plugins, adapters, tools, examples and others. Hence the creation of Better Auth Kit.

## License

Everything in the Better Auth Kit project is licensed under the [MIT license](https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/LICENSE).

---

# API

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/libraries/tests.mdx

title: "@better-auth-kit/tests"
description: A collection of utilities to help you test your Better-Auth plugins.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/tests" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/libraries/tests" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/tests" />

If you're developing a custom plugin for Better-Auth, you may need to test it. This library is intended to provide utilities to help you test your plugins.

<Callout type="info">
This library currently is pulled out from the main Better-Auth package, but is intended to provide more features in the future.

<Steps>
<Step>

## Installation

```package-install
@better-auth-kit/tests
```

</Step>
<Step>

## Usage

Initiate a better-auth instance, and then create a test instance.

```ts title="my-plugin.test.ts"
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { bearer } from "better-auth/plugins/bearer";
import { getTestInstance } from "@better-auth-kit/tests";
import { myPlugin, myClientPlugin } from "./my-plugin.ts";// [!code highlight]

// Create a better-auth instance
const auth = betterAuth({
	database: new Database(), // Your database adapter // [!code highlight]
	plugins: [bearer(), myPlugin()], // [!code highlight]
	secret: "better-auth.secret",
	emailAndPassword: {
		enabled: true,
	},
	rateLimit: {
		enabled: false,
	},
	advanced: {
		disableCSRFCheck: true,
		cookies: {},
	},
})

const { auth, db, client, testUser, signInWithTestUser } = await getTestInstance(// [!code highlight]
	auth,// [!code highlight]
	{// [!code highlight]
		clientOptions: {// [!code highlight]
			plugins: [myClientPlugin()],// [!code highlight]
		},// [!code highlight]
	},// [!code highlight]
);// [!code highlight]
```
</Step>
<Step>

## Begin testing!

You can now use the test APIs to test your plugin:

```ts title="my-plugin.test.ts"
// Your test user is already created
const { headers, user } = await signInWithTestUser();

describe("My Plugin", () => {
	it("should do something cool", async () => {
		const result = await client.myPlugin.doSomethingCool();
        
		expect(result).toBe(true);
	});
});
```

Then, start Vitest!

```bash
vitest foobar
```

</Step>

</Steps>

<div className="h-10" />

# API

## `getTestInstance`

Optionally takes two arguments, the first is the options for the `betterAuth` instance, the second is the options for the test instance itself.

You can configure the betterAuth client instance inside the second argument.

```ts
const {
	auth,
	db,
	client,
	testUser,
	signInWithTestUser,
	signInWithUser,
	cookieSetter,
	customFetchImpl,
	sessionSetter,
}  = await getTestInstance(
	auth, // Your better-auth instance
	{
		clientOptions: {
            // Client options
			plugins: [myClientPlugin()],
		},
	},
);
```

### Options

- `clientOptions` - The options for the Better-Auth client instance.
- `port` - The baseURL port for the better-auth instance.
- `disableTestUser` - Whether to disable the test user.
- `testUser` - The test user to use for the test instance.
- `testWith` - The database to use for the test instance. (`sqlite`, `postgres`, `mongodb`, `mysql`)

### Methods

- `client` - The Better-Auth client instance.
- `testUser` - The premade test user.
- `signInWithTestUser` - Sign in with the premade test user.
- `signInWithUser` - Sign in with a custom user.
- `cookieSetter` - Set the cookie for the test instance.
- `customFetchImpl` - The custom fetch implementation for the test instance.
- `sessionSetter` - Set the session for the test instance.

#### `client`

The Better-Auth client instance.

#### `testUser`

The premade test user.

#### `signInWithTestUser`

```ts
const { headers, user } = await signInWithTestUser();
```

#### `signInWithUser`

```ts
const { headers, user } = await signInWithUser(email, password);
```

#### `cookieSetter`

Useful for getting the session of a successful sign in and applying that to a new headers object's cookie.

```ts
const headers = new Headers();
await client.signIn.email(
    {
        email: testUser.email,
        password: testUser.password,
    },
    {
        onSuccess: cookieSetter(headers),
    },
);
```

#### `customFetchImpl`

By default, when using the auth client, we make a fetch request to the better-auth server whenever you call an endpoint.
However, you can optionally provide the `customFetchImpl` to bypass this and it will skip the fetch request to the better-auth server, and instead directly invoke the endpoint on the server.

```ts
const client = createAuthClient({
	baseURL: "http://localhost:3000",
	fetchOptions: {
		customFetchImpl,
	},
});
```

#### `sessionSetter`

Useful for getting the session from the response of a successful sign in and applying that to a new headers object.

```ts
const headers = new Headers();
await client.signIn.email(
    {
        email: testUser.email,
        password: testUser.password,
    },
    {
        onSuccess: sessionSetter(headers),
    },
);

const response = await client.listSessions({
    fetchOptions: {
        headers,
    },
});
```

#### `db`

The database adapter.

```ts title="example"
await db.create({
	model: "sometable",
	data: {
		hello: "world"
	},
});
```

To stay up-to-date with the current progress of Better-Auth-Kit, you can track our [roadmap here](/roadmap).

## Plugins

- [Waitlist](/docs/plugins/waitlist) - A plugin to create a waitlist for your users. (Coming Soon)
- [Reverify](/docs/plugins/reverify) - A plugin to reverify a user's identity.
- [Legal Consent](/docs/plugins/legal-consent) - A plugin to collect legal consent from your users. (Coming Soon)
- [Blockade](/docs/plugins/blockade) - A plugin to blacklist or whitelist users from accessing your application. (Coming Soon)
- [Shutdown](/docs/plugins/shutdown) - A plugin to stop signins or signups at any moment, such as for maintenance. (Coming Soon)
- [Feedback](/docs/plugins/feedback) - A plugin to collect feedback from your users.

## Libraries

- [Admin Dashboard](/docs/libraries/admin-dashboard) - A library to help you get started with the Admin Dashboard. (Coming Soon)
- [Better-Auth-Kit Tests](/docs/libraries/tests) - A library to assist you during Better-Auth plugin testing.

## Adapters

- [Convex DB](/docs/adapters/convex) - An adapter to use Convex DB as your database with Better-Auth.
- [Pocketbase DB](/docs/adapters/pocketbase) - An adapter to use Pocketbase as your database with Better-Auth. (Coming Soon)
- [Firestore DB](/docs/adapters/firestore) - An adapter to use Firebase's Firestore as your database with Better-Auth. (Coming Soon)

## Better-Auth-Kit CLI

A CLI tool to help your with your Better-Auth development.

- [UI Components](/docs/cli/ui-components) - Generate UI components using the ShadCN registry.
- [Seed](/docs/cli/seed) - Seed your Better-Auth database with deterministic, yet realistic, fake data.
- [Database Explorer](/docs/cli/database-explorer) - A Better-Auth powered database explorer and schema visualizer.
- [Dashboard](/docs/cli/dashboard) - A Clerk-like dashboard for your Better-Auth project. (Coming Soon)

Read more about the [Better-Auth-Kit CLI](/docs/cli/information).

# app-invite.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/plugins/app-invite.mdx

title: App Invite
description: Invite users to your application and allow them to sign up.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/app-invite" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/plugins/app-invite" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/app-invite" />

The App Invite plugin enables you to invite users to your application through email invitations. It supports two types of invitations:

- **Personal Invitations**: Targeted to specific email addresses, ensuring only the intended recipient can use the invitation
- **Public Invitations**: Can be used by multiple users, making it ideal for open sign-up scenarios

This plugin is particularly useful for invite-only applications.

<Callout>
  This plugin was implemented as a PR for better-auth, however it is not yet merged.
  We've copied the implementation here to allow you to use it in your projects, until it is merged, in which case we will deprecate
  this plugin. And you may directly import the plugin from `better-auth` instead.

  Any issues or feedback should be directed to the active PR [here](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/1436).

## Installation

<Steps>
    <Step>
    ### Install the plugin
    ```package-install
    npm install @better-auth-kit/app-invite
    ```
    </Step>

    <Step>
    ### Add the plugin to your auth config

    To use the App Invite plugin, add it to your auth config.

    ```ts title="auth.ts"
    import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
    import { appInvite } from "@better-auth-kit/app-invite" // [!code highlight]

    export const auth = betterAuth({
        // ... other config options
        plugins: [
            appInvite({ // [!code highlight]
                // required for personal invites // [!code highlight]
                sendInvitationEmail: (data) => { // [!code highlight]
                    // ... send invitation to the user // [!code highlight]
                } // [!code highlight]
            }) // [!code highlight]
        ]
    })
    ```

    </Step>
    <Step>
    ### Add the client plugin

    Include the App Invite client plugin in your authentication client instance.

    ```ts title="auth-client.ts"
    import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client"
    import { appInviteClient } from "@better-auth-kit/app-invite/client" // [!code highlight]

    const authClient = createAuthClient({
        plugins: [
            appInviteClient() // [!code highlight]
        ]
    })
    ```

    </Step>

    <Step>
    ### Run migrations

    This plugin adds an additional table to the database. [Click here to see the schema](#schema)

    ```package-install
    npx @better-auth/cli migrate
    ```

    or generate

    ```package-install
    npx @better-auth/cli generate
    ```

    </Step>
</Steps>

## Usage

To add members to the application, we first need to send an invitation to the user. 
The user will receive an email with the invitation link. Once the user accepts the invitation, they will be signed up to the application.

### Setup Invitation Email

For personal invites to work we first need to provide `sendInvitationEmail` to the `better-auth` instance.
This function is responsible for sending the invitation email to the user.

You'll need to construct and send the invitation link to the user. The link should include the invitation ID,
which will be used with the acceptInvitation function when the user clicks on it.

This is only required for personal invites. Sharing public invitations is up to the inviter.

```ts title="auth.ts"
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { appInvite } from "@better-auth-kit/app-invite";
import { sendAppInvitation } from "./email";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    appInvite({
      async sendInvitationEmail(data) {
        const inviteLink = `https://example.com/accept-invitation/${data.id}`;
        sendAppInvitation({
          name: data.name,
          email: data.email,
          invitedByUsername: data.inviter.name,
          invitedByEmail: data.inviter.email,
          inviteLink,
        });
      },
    }),
  ],
});
```

### Send Invitation

To invite users to the app, you can use the `invite` function provided by the client.
the `invite` function takes an object with the following properties:

- `email`: The email address of the user to invite. Leave empty to create a public invitation.

- `resend`: A boolean value that determines whether to resend the invitation email,
if the user is already invited. Defaults to `false`

- `domainWhitelist`: An optional comma separated list of domains that allows public invitations
to be accepted only from approved domains.

```ts title="invitation.ts"
await authClient.inviteUser({
  email: "test@email.com",
});
```

### Accept Invitation

When a user receives an invitation email, they can click on the invitation link to accept the invitation.
The link should include the invitation ID, which will be used to accept the invitation.

```ts title="auth-client.ts"
await authClient.acceptInvitation({
  invitationId: "invitation-id",
  name: "John Doe", // overridden if predefined in the invitation
  email: "test@email.com", // must be set for public invites
  password: "password123456",
  // ... additional user data
});
```

### Update Invitation Status

To update the status of invitations you can use the `acceptInvitation`, `rejectInvitation`, `cancelInvitation`
function provided by the client. The functions take the invitation id as an argument.

```ts title="auth-client.ts"
// cancel invitation (by default only the inviter can cancel invitations)
await authClient.cancelInvitation({
  invitationId: "invitation-id",
});

// reject invitation (this is only available for personal invites)
await authClient.rejectInvitation({
  invitationId: "invitation-id",
});
```

### Get Invitation

To get an invitation you can use the `getAppInvitation` function provided by the client. You need to provide the
invitation id as a query parameter.

```ts title="auth-client"
await authClient.getAppInvitation({
  query: {
    id: params.id,
  },
});
```

### List Invitations

Allows an user to list all invitations issued by themself.

```ts title="auth-client"
await authClient.listInvitations({
  query: {
    limit: 10,
  },
});
```

By default 100 invitations are returned. You can adjust the limit and offset using the following query parameters:

- `searchField`: The field to search on, which can be `email`, `name` or `domainWhitelist`.
- `searchOperator`: The operator to use for the search. It can be `contains`, `starts_with`, or `ends_with`.
- `searchValue`: The value to search for.
- `limit`: The number of invitations to return.
- `offset`: The number of invitations to skip.
- `sortBy`: The field to sort the invitations by.
- `sortDirection`: The direction to sort the invitations by. Defaults to `asc`.
- `filterField`: The field to filter the invitations by.
- `filterOperator`: The operator to use for the filter. It can be `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt` or `gte`.
- `filterValue`: The value to filter the invitations by.

```ts title="Example"
await authClient.listInvitations({
  query: {
    searchField: "domainWhitelist",
    searchOperator: "contains",
    searchValue: "example.com",
    limit: 10,
    offset: 0,
    sortBy: "createdAt",
    sortDirection: "desc",
    filterField: "expiresAt",
    filterOperator: "lt",
    filterValue: new Date().toISOString(),
  },
});
```

## Schema

The plugin requires an additional table in the database.

Table Name: `appInvitation`

<SchemaDemo plugin="appInvite" includeDefaultUser focus="appInvitation" schema={{
    appInvitation: {
      fields: {
        name: {
        type: "string",
        required: false,
      },
      email: {
        type: "string",
        required: false,
      },
      inviterId: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
        references: {
            model: "user",
            field: "id",
        }
      },
      status: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
      },
      domainWhitelist: {
        type: "string",
        required: true
      },
      expiresAt: {
        type: "date",
        required: true
      },
      createdAt: {
        type: "date",
        required: true,
      },
      }
  }
}} />

Fields:

- `id`: Unique identifier for each invitation
- `name`: The name of the user
- `email`: The email address of the user
- `inviterId`: The ID of the inviter
- `status`: The status of the invitation
- `domainWhitelist`: A comma separated whitelist of domains for a public invitation
- `expiresAt`: Timestamp of when the invitation expires
- `createdAt`: Timestamp of when the invitation was created

## Options

**allowUserToCreateInvitation**: `boolean` | `((user: User, type: "personal" | "public") => Promise<boolean> | boolean)` - A function that determines whether a user can create invite others. By defaults it's `true`. You can set it to `false` to restrict users from creating invitations.

**allowUserToCancelInvitation**: `(data: { user: User, invitation: AppInvitation }) => Promise<boolean> | boolean` - A functon that determines whether a user can cancel inivtations. By default the user can only cancel invites created by them. You can set it to `false` to restrict users from canceling invitations.

**invitationExpiresIn**: `number` - How long the invitation link is valid for in seconds. By default, it's 48 hours (2 days).

**sendInvitationEmail**: `async (data) => Promise<void>` - A function that sends an invitation email to the user. This is only required for personal invitations.

**autoSignIn**: A boolean value that determines whether to prevent automatic sign-up when accepting an invitation. Defaults to `false`.

**$Infer.AdditionalFields**: Allows you to infer additional data for the user. This option is available in the client plugin aswell.

## Shout out

Big shout out to <GithubUser>jslno</GithubUser> for the initial implementation of the app invite plugin. ❤️

# feedback.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/plugins/feedback.mdx

title: Feedback
description: Allow users to submit feedback about your application.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/feedback" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/plugins/feedback" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/feedback" />

The Feedback plugin allows users to submit feedback about your application. By default, only authenticated users can submit feedback, but this can be configured.

<Steps>
  <Step>
        ### 1. Install the plugin

        ```package-install
        @better-auth-kit/feedback
        ```

  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### 2. Initialize the plugin

    ```ts title="auth.ts"
    import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
    import { feedback } from "@better-auth-kit/feedback";

    export const auth = betterAuth({
      plugins: [
        feedback(),
      ],
    });
    ```

    ```ts title="auth-client.ts"
    import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth";
    import { feedbackClient } from "@better-auth-kit/feedback/client";

    export const authClient = createAuthClient({
      plugins: [feedbackClient()],
    });
    ```

  </Step>
  <Step>
  ### 3. Run migrations

  Make sure to run migrations after configuring the plugin.

<Tabs items={["migrate", "generate"]}>
<Tab value="migrate">
```package-install
npx @better-auth/cli migrate
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="generate">
```package-install
npx @better-auth/cli generate
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>
<span className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>Learn more about the migrate/generate commands [here](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/concepts/cli#generate).</span>

  </Step>
  <Step>
    ### 4. Use the plugin

    <Tabs items={["client", "server"]}>
      <Tab value="client">
        ```ts
        // Submit feedback (requires logged-in user by default)
        await authClient.feedback.submit({
          text: "This is my feedback about the application"
        });
        ```
      </Tab>
      <Tab value="server">
        ```ts
        // Submit feedback
        await auth.api.submitFeedback({
          body: {
            text: "This is my feedback about the application"
          }
        });
        ```
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>

  </Step>
</Steps>

<div className="h-10" />

## Configuration Options

You can customize the Feedback plugin with the following options:

```ts
feedback({
  /* Text length constraints */
  minLength: 10, // Minimum text length (default: 10)
  maxLength: 500, // Maximum text length (default: 500)

  /* User submission controls */
  feedbackLimit: 5, // Limit number of feedbacks per user (optional)
  requireAuth: true, // Whether authentication is required (default: true)
  canSubmitFeedback: (user) => {
    // To add to control who can submit feedback
    // Ex: only allow organization owners
    return user.role === "owner";
  },

  /* To customize schema field names */
  schema: {
    feedback: {
      modelName: "feedbackEntries", // Rename the model
      fields: {
        userId: "authorId", // Rename fields
        text: "message",
        createdAt: "submittedAt",
      },
    },
  },

  /* To add additional fields to the schema */
  additionalFields: {
    category: { type: "string", required: true, default: "General" },
    rating: { type: "number", required: true, default: -1 },
  },

  /* To add callback function that gets executed server-side when feedback is submitted */
  onFeedback: async ({ feedback, user }) => {
    console.log(
      `Feedback submitted by ${user?.email ?? "USER UNKNOWN"}: ${feedback}`
    );

    // Example: Send ourselves an email using Resend
    await resend.emails.send({
      from: "noreply@yourapp.com",
      to: "owner@yourapp.com",
      cc: user?.email ? [user.email] : undefined, // You can even include the user
      subject: user?.email
        ? `Feedback submitted by ${user.email}`
        : "Anonymous feedback submitted",
      html: `<h1>Feedback submitted by ${user?.email ?? "Anonymous"}:</h1><p>${feedback.text}</p>`,
    });
  },
});
```

## Schema

<SchemaDemo plugin="feedback" includeDefaultUser schema={{
  feedback: {
    fields: {
      userId: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
        references: {
          model: "user",
          field: "id",
        }
      },
      text: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
      },
      createdAt: {
        type: "date",
        required: true,
      },
    }
  }
}} />

Fields:

- `id`: Unique identifier for the feedback entry
- `userId`: ID of the user who submitted the feedback (optional if `requireAuth` is `false`)
- `text`: The feedback content (controlled by minLength/maxLength)
- `createdAt`: Timestamp when the feedback was submitted

# legal-consent.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/plugins/legal-consent.mdx

title: Legal Consent
description: Ensure legal compliance by requiring users to accept terms of service, privacy policy, age verification, and other consent requirements during sign-up.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/legal-consent" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/plugins/legal-consent" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/legal-consent" />

<Callout type="warn">
    There is an existing bug, we're investigating it.

In some cases, you may need to require your users to accept certain compliances before they can sign up.
The purpose of this plugin is to provide a way to keep record, or evidence, of the user's consent to the compliances.

Supported compliances include: **Terms of Service**, **Privacy Policy**, 
**Age Verification**, **Marketing Consent**, and **Cookie Consent**.

Currently, we provide both a basic form of record keeping, which is a boolean field in the user model indicating 
if the user has accepted the compliance, and optionally the ability to save the version of the consent form which the user agreed to. In the future, we plan to expand this by providing the option to enable more detailed
record keeping, such as timestamps, IP addresses, device information, and more, saved in a separate table.
This makes to be better evidence of the user's consent to the compliances.

{/* <Callout type="warn">
    This plugin does not come with UI, this is purely functionality.
    We recommend checking out our [UI components](/docs/tools/ui-components) registry to implement shadcn styled components.
</Callout> */}

<Steps>

<Step>
### 1. Install the plugin

```package-install
npm install @better-auth-kit/legal-consent
```
</Step>

<Step>
### 2. Initialize the plugin

```ts title="auth.ts"
import { legalConsent } from "@better-auth-kit/legal-consent";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    legalConsent({
      requireTOS: true,
      requirePrivacyPolicy: true,
      requireMarketingConsent: true,
      requireCookieConsent: true,
    }),
  ],
});
```
</Step>

<Step>
### 3. Run Migrations

Make sure to run migrations after configuring the plugin.

<Tabs items={["migrate", "generate"]}>
<Tab value="migrate">
```package-install
npx @better-auth/cli migrate
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="generate">
```package-install
npx @better-auth/cli generate
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>
<span className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>Learn more about the migrate/generate commands [here](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/concepts/cli#generate).</span>

</Step>
<Step>
### 4. Sign up methods

Add the following methods to your sign up page.

<Tabs items={["server", "client"]}>

<Tab value="server">
```ts
auth.api.signUpEmail({
 body: {
    email: "some_email@example.com",
    password: "some_password",
    tosAccepted: true,
    privacyPolicyAccepted: true,
    ageVerified: true,
    marketingConsentAccepted: true,
    cookieConsentAccepted: true,
 }
});
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="client">
```ts
authClient.signUp.email({
  email: "some_email@example.com",
  password: "some_password",
  tosAccepted: true,
  privacyPolicyAccepted: true,
  ageVerified: true,
  marketingConsentAccepted: true,
  cookieConsentAccepted: true,
});
```
</Tab>

</Tabs>

<Callout type="warn">
    The types may not appear in your IDE for the signUp method, this is a limitation of Better Auth. 
    Once you enable a given legal consent, you should be fine to pass that value into the sign up method and safely ignore the type error.

    Note: You do not need to pass all the legal consent values, only the ones you enabled.
</Step>

</Steps>

<Comprehensive>
## What does it do?

By utilizing the `legalConsent` plugin, you can require the following legal consents on your sign-up routes:

- Terms of Service
- Privacy Policy
- Age Verification
- Marketing Consent
- Cookie Consent

Whenever a user signs up, the plugin requires you to pass additional data to the `signup` method.
The data can vary depending on the legal consent requirements you have set.
For example, if you require the user to accept the terms of service, you must pass `tosAccepted: true` to the `signup` method.
After the plugin has verified the given data is all valid, it will pass those legal consent values to the user data that will be created.
</Comprehensive>

## Options

### Legal Compliance Configuration

You can enable the following legal compliance options:

```ts
legalConsent({
  tosAccepted: true,
  privacyPolicyAccepted: true,
  ageVerified: true,
  marketingConsentAccepted: true,
  cookieConsentAccepted: true
});
```

You can also choose to save the version of the legal consent agreement.

```ts
legalConsent({
  tosVersion: "1.0",
  privacyPolicyVersion: "1.0",
  ageVerificationVersion: "1.0",
  marketingConsentVersion: "1.0",
  cookieConsentVersion: "1.0",
});
```

If the version is provided, it will save the version of the legal consent agreement in the user model. 
Otherwise, it will save the agreement as a boolean.

<Callout>
If you had updated the plugin to include versions, make sure to run migrations again! 
By default, the plugin will save the boolean value. By adding the version, it will save the version string.

### Configuring the schema

You can configure the name of these fields by passing the `schema` option to the plugin.

```ts
legalConsent({
  schema: {
    userModelName: "user",
    tosAccepted: "tosAccepted",
    privacyPolicyAccepted: "privacyPolicyAccepted",
    ageVerified: "ageVerified",
    marketingConsentAccepted: "marketingConsentAccepted",
    cookieConsentAccepted: "cookieConsentAccepted",
  },
});
```

## Schema

Table: `user`

<Callout type="warn">
Note: Not all keys will be in the table as it depends on if you enabled each compliance, as well as if you changed the name of a given schema field.

<SchemaDemo plugin="legal-consent" includeDefaultUser focus="user" schema={{
  user: {
    fields: {
      tosAccepted: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
      },
      privacyPolicyAccepted: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
      },
      ageVerified: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
      },
      marketingConsentAccepted: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
      },
      cookieConsentAccepted: {
        type: "string",
        required: true,
      },
    }
  }
}} />

Fields:

- `tosAccepted`: Wether the user accepted the TOS.
- `privacyPolicyAccepted`: Wether the user accepted the privacy policy.
- `ageVerified`: Wether the user verified their age.
- `marketingConsentAccepted`: Wether the user accepted the marketing consent.
- `cookieConsentAccepted`: Wether the user accepted the cookie consent.

# profile-image.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/plugins/profile-image.mdx

title: Profile Image
description: Upload, delete, and manage profile pictures for your users.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/profile-image" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/plugins/profile-image" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/profile-image" />

<Callout type="warn">
  This plugin is currently in development we do not recommend using it just yet!

This plugin allow your users to upload, delete, and manage their profile pictures.
Additionally, it provides a way to store the profile picture in a storage provider of your choice, set up validation rules, and more.

<Steps>
  <Step>
        ### 1. Install the plugin

        ```package-install
        @better-auth-kit/profile-image
        ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### 2. Initialize the plugin

    Make sure you have defined `UPLOADTHING_API_KEY` in your environment variables, or define it as the `apiKey` property of the `UTApi` instance.

    ```ts title="auth.ts"
    import { profileImage, UploadThingProvider } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image";
    import { UTApi } from "uploadthing/server";
    import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";

    const utApi = new UTApi();
    const provider = new UploadThingProvider(utApi);

    export const auth = betterAuth({ // [!code highlight]
      plugins: [profileImage({ storageProvider: provider })],// [!code highlight]
    });// [!code highlight]
    ```

    ```ts title="auth-client.ts"
    import { profileImageClient } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image/client";
    import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client";

    export const authClient = createAuthClient({// [!code highlight]
      plugins: [profileImageClient()],// [!code highlight]
    });// [!code highlight]
    ```

    <Callout type="info">
      Want to use another storage provider? Check out the [storage providers](#storage-providers) section.
  </Step>
  <Step>
    ### 3. Use the plugin

    <Tabs items={["Basic Example", "React Example"]}>
      <Tab value="Basic Example">
        ```ts
        import { fileToBase64 } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image";
        import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client";

        const { data } = await authClient.profileImage.upload({// [!code highlight]
          image: someFileOrBlob,// [!code highlight]
        });// [!code highlight]

        const { url, key } = data; // URL and key of the uploaded image.
      ```
      </Tab>
      <Tab value="React Example">
        ```tsx
        function UploadProfileImage() {
          const [image, setImage] = useState<File | null>(null);

          const handleFileChange = async (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            const file = e.target.files?.[0];
            if (!file) return;
            setImage(file);
          };

          const uploadImage = async () => {
            if (!image) return;
            const { data, error } = await authClient.profileImage.upload({
              image: blob,
            });
            if(data){
              console.log(`Successfully uploaded image to ${data.image.url}`);
            }else{
              console.error(`Something went wrong:`, error);
            }
          };

          return (
            <div>
              <Label htmlFor="image-upload">Upload Image</Label>
              <Input
                id="image-upload"
                type="file"
                accept="image/*"
                onChange={handleFileChange}
              />
              <Button onClick={uploadImage}>Upload Image</Button>
            </div>
          );
        }

        ```
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Usage

### Uploading an image

Upload an image to the user's profile.

```ts
import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client";

// Get a file or blob from somewhere, e.g. from a file input.
const someFileOrBlob = new File([], "image.png", { type: "image/png" });

const { data, error } = await authClient.profileImage.upload({ // [!code highlight]
  image: someFileOrBlob, // [!code highlight]
}); // [!code highlight]

if(data){
  console.log(`Successfully uploaded image to ${data.url}`);
}else{
  console.error(`Something went wrong:`, error);
}
```

<Callout>
The profile image upload functionality is currently only supported through the auth-client.
Server-side auth instance support is still in development and testing.

#### Upload a compressed image

By uploading a compressed image, you can reduce the size of the image by lowering the quality of the image, and converting it to JPEG
before it is uploaded to the server.

If you're using a set of cusom `allowedTypes` in the plugin options, you should ensure to include `image/jpeg` in the list.
This is because the `compressImage` function will convert the image to JPEG.

```ts
import { compressImage } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image/client";

// Get a file or blob from somewhere, e.g. from a file input.
const someFileOrBlob = new File([], "image.png", { type: "image/png" });

const compressedImage = await compressImage(someFileOrBlob, 0.7);// [!code highlight]
if(!compressedImage) return;

const { data, error } = await authClient.profileImage.upload({
  image: compressedImage,
});
```

<Callout type="warn">
  This only works on the browser, since it requires the `createImageBitmap` API.

### Deleting an image

Delete the user's profile image.

<Tabs items={["client", "server"]}>
  <Tab value="client">
    ```ts
    import { authClient } from "@/lib/auth-client";

    const { error } = await authClient.profileImage.delete();
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="server">
    ```ts
    import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";

    await auth.api.deleteProfileImage({ headers: await headers() });
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>
## Plugin Options

```ts
import { profileImage } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    profileImage({
      // A storage provider adapter, see the storage providers section below.
      storageProvider: provider, 
       // Maximum file size in bytes, default is 5MB
      maxSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
      // Allowed file types, default is ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp"]
      allowedTypes: ["image/jpeg", "image/webp"], 
      canUploadImage: (session) => {
        // A function that returns a boolean, default is `true`.
        return session.user.id === "123"; 
      },
      onImageUploaded: ({ profileImage, user }) => {
        // A function that is called when the image is uploaded, default is `undefined`.
      },
      // Optional array of trusted image origins, default is undefined. If undefined, any origin is trusted.
      trustedImageOrigins: ["https://example.com"],
    }),
  ],
});
```

## Security

Any attempts at modifying or creating a user's `image` will run through validation checks to ensure they're a valid URL,
and are part of the `trustedImageOrigins` if enabled in the plugin config.

We recommend to set up a trusted image origins, to prevent users from having any way of
setting their profile picture to an image from an untrusted origin.

```ts
export const auth = betterAuth({
  plugins: [
    profileImage({
      trustedImageOrigins: ["https://example.com"],
    }),
  ],
});
```

<Callout type="warn">
  If you're using the UploadThing provider, we recommend adding `https://<YOUR_APP_ID>.ufs.sh` to the trusted image origins.

## Optimizations

To optimize the performance of an image upload, you have several options:

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Compress the image on the client side">
    You can compress the image on the client side using the `compressImage` function.
    This will reduce the size of the image by lowering the quality of the image, and converting it to JPEG
     before it is uploaded to the server.

    <Callout type="warn">
    If you're using a set of cusom `allowedTypes` in the plugin options, you should ensure to include `image/jpeg` in the list.
    This is because the `compressImage` function will convert the image to JPEG.
    
    ```ts
    import { compressImage } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image/client";
    ```

    ```ts
    // 0.7 is the default quality.
    const compressedImage = await compressImage(imageBlob, 0.7); 

    // `null` is returned if the image could not be created for any reason.
    if(!compressedImage) return; 

    // Upload the compressed image to the server.
    const { data, error } = await authClient.profileImage.upload(compressedImage);
    ```
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Enforce a maximum file size">
      You can enforce a maximum file size in the plugin options, but also add checks on the client side to ensure the
      image is not too large before uploading.

      ```tsx
      const handleFileChange = async (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
        const file = e.target.files?.[0];
        if (!file) return;
        if(file.size > 1000000) { // 1MB
          // Display an error message to the user.
        }
      };
      ```

      Here's how you can enforce a maximum file size in the plugin options, like so:

      ```ts
      import { profileImage } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image";

      export const auth = betterAuth({
        plugins: [
          profileImage({
            maxSize: 1000000, // 1MB, default is 5MB
          }),
        ],
      });
      ```
    </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Enforce specific file types">
    By forcing the user to only upload JPEG, or WebP images, you can reduce the image size versus uploading PNGs.

    You can run checks on the client side to ensure the image is of the correct type before uploading, like so:

    ```tsx
    const handleFileChange = async (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
      const file = e.target.files?.[0];
      if (!file) return;
      if(!file.type.includes("image")) {
        // Display an error message to the user.
      }
    };
    ```

    And ensure to enable the `allowedTypes` option in the plugin options, like so:

    ```ts
    import { profileImage } from "@better-auth-kit/profile-image";

    export const auth = betterAuth({
      plugins: [
        profileImage({
          allowedTypes: ["image/jpeg", "image/webp"],
        }),
      ],
    });
    ```
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Storage Providers

Right now, we only support [UploadThing](https://uploadthing.com), however we plan to support more storage providers in the future.

We hope to add these storage providers in the future:

- [Cloudflare R2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/)
- [AWS S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/)
- [Google Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage)
- [Azure Blob Storage](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/storage/blobs)
- [Cloud Storage for Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage)

Feel free to help us by contributing any of these storage providers,
we greatly appriciate any effort towards improving the Better Auth ecosystem!

## Future plans
We're actively working on expanding the plugin's capabilities, including features like profile picture history 
and integration with additional [storage providers](#storage-providers).
Your feedback and contributions are invaluable to us -
if you have suggestions or would like to help implement new features, we'd love to hear from you through issues or pull requests.

## Shoutout

Big thanks to <GithubUser>zpg6</GithubUser> for the plugin idea and the initial implementation. ❤️

# reverify.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/plugins/reverify.mdx

title: Reverify
description: Prompt the user to re-verify their identity by providing their password for revalidation.

<StatsBadge npmPackage="@better-auth-kit/reverify" />
<GithubButton url="https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/tree/main/packages/plugins/reverify" />
<NpmButton url="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@better-auth-kit/reverify" />

The purpose of this plugin is to allow the user to re-verify their identity without modifying their current session.
An example use case is before deleting an API key, you would want to re-verify the user's
identity to ensure they are the one deleting the key.

<Callout>
  This plugin is not for the purpose of refreshing a session, if you want to refresh a session you can use any of the sign-in related methods.

<Steps>
  <Step>
        ### 1. Install the plugin

        ```package-install
        @better-auth-kit/reverify
        ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### 2. Initialize the plugin

    ```ts title="auth.ts"
    import { reverify } from "@better-auth-kit/reverify";

    export const auth = betterAuth({
      plugins: [reverify()],
    });
    ```

    ```ts title="auth-client.ts"
    import { reverifyClient } from "@better-auth-kit/reverify/client";

    export const authClient = createAuthClient({
      plugins: [reverifyClient()],
    });
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step>
    ### 3. Use the plugin

    <Tabs items={["client", "server"]}>
      <Tab value="client">
        ```ts
        const { data } = await client.reverify.password({
          password: "some-password",
        });
        
        const isValid = data?.valid;
        ```
      </Tab>
      <Tab value="server">
        ```ts
        const data = await auth.api.reverifyPassword({
          body: {
            password: "some-password",
          },
          headers,
        });

        const isValid = data?.valid;
        ```
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>
  </Step>
</Steps>

<div className="h-10" />

# how-to-think-about-better-auth.mdx

Source: https://github.com/ping-maxwell/better-auth-kit/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/random-other-stuff/how-to-think-about-better-auth.mdx

title: How to think about Better Auth
description: A short guide to help you understand how to think about Better Auth

## 1. Better Auth lives on the server, but also the client?

Better Auth comes with two instances. Your server auth instance (`auth`), and a client auth instance (`authClient`). Your server auth instance is where Better Auth primarily lives, it provides the auth endpoints for the client auth instance to call.

Using the `authClient` would make a request to an endpoint provided by Better Auth, however if you use the server `auth` instance, it would directly call the function for that endpoint, instead of making a request.

This means that if you’re on the front-end, you should use the `authClient` instance, otherwise you should use server `auth` instance.

## 1. Better Auth is basically a router

Better Auth at it’s core is a bunch of endpoints connected to any framework you use. These endpoints are considered your auth endpoints, and can do things such as creating a user, getting a user sessions, or anything else capable in Better Auth. When you add a plugin, you’re essentially adding more endpoints.

## 2. Endpoints are methods

All endpoints gathered from Better Auth itself or plugins, are all accessible through your auth instance. For example, the sign up endpoint (`/api/auth/sign-up/email`) is just a method you can call in your `authClient` - `authClient.signUp.email` , or similarly on your `auth` instance - `auth.api.signUpEmail` 

## 3. Better Auth handles your database, but you should too.

Every database call from Better Auth runs through schemas which are customisable to your liking. By default we provide schemas for models such as `user`, `session`, `account`, and potentially others. Whenever you add a plugin, it can optionally include additional schemas which can alter your current schema. All of the plugin schemas and the default schema by Better Auth are combined into one, and this combined schema tells us how your database tables and fields are defined.

Endpoints could add, update, delete or do anything with you database. Often times, a plugin which is supposedly in control of specific models (eg `organization` plugin handles `organization` table, `member` table, etc) would provide most of the interactions you can do to the database that may relate to that table. However there can be cases where there isn’t a provided endpoint, in which case you can freely use your ORM to directly call your database to do said action. It’s important to remember that your database tables is just as accessible to Better Auth as it is to you.

## 4. Plugins

At it’s core, plugins essentially adds additional endpoints, as well as potentially modifying your Better Auth schema. Additionally, they can also have hooks or middleware’s to intercept auth endpoint requests to run authorization checks, modify data, or anything else as needed.

Plugins are quite simple, and when put together, allows the end-developer (That’s you!) to run one function and sit back and relax. For example, the `api-key` plugin has an endpoint to create an API key:

<img src="/docs/example-plugin-flow.png" alt="API Key Plugin" />

Pretty simple, right?

## That's about it.

Of course there are a lot of things that Better Auth can do, including hooks, DB hooks, and other stuff, however the gist is here.
Better Auth is designed to be extremely flexible and extendable, and that's the main idea to take away from this. I highly recommend 
reading through the [Better Auth docs](https://better-auth.com/docs) to get a more in-depth understanding of what you can do with Better Auth.
